asked.quote: Can you analyse the token usage on before and after the board's update ? The goal would be to implement scripts into the kit that automatically track token usage, tool use, agent use, etc. in every conversation - parts, orchestrator, reviewer, etc., without using any tokens themselves, for proper comparison and optimization pre/post kit updates and changes.

part, median $ per 100 lines changed: $1.33 (n 96) vs $0.92 (n 20), -31%; commits per session 6 vs 5.5

orchestrators O40-O48 vs O49-O53: median $24.04 vs $40.32 per session (+68%), 119k vs 207k output, $3.3 vs $6.3 per hour
whole project, window vs window: $25.69 vs $22.63 per part (33 and 19 parts), $286 vs $443 per day

body:
**A part now does about the same work for less: 31% less per 100 lines changed, with about as many commits (median 6 before, 5.5 after). An orchestrator costs more per session (+57%) and per commit (+63%).** Every session from now on records its own row, including its work, with no model call (the `kit_usage.py` hook). To judge a kit change, run `kit.py usage compare --before <commit> --after <commit>`.

## Source
Measured from the platform's own record of every Harmonize cloud session (claude-code-remote `get_session` usage: input, output, cache read, cache write tokens and `cost_usd`): 254 sessions with usage out of 289 listed, 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-24. Nothing is estimated. How they were fetched: no script can reach claude-code-remote. It is a tool of the model's harness, with no HTTP API inside a container. So one Haiku subagent called `list_sessions`, then `get_session` once per session (355 calls), and wrote the records to a JSONL file. `usage.py import-ccr` read that file. The agent cost $2.17, measured from its own transcript. This is needed once, for sessions that ran before the hook existed. A cloud session from now on has its transcript on its own container, where the hook reads it. The rows (no titles or text) are in `docs/CL37-sessions.jsonl`; every table below is rebuilt by `python3 -I scripts/usage.py compare --before 2026-11-23T00:27:22+00:00 --after 2026-11-23T01:25:19+00:00 --rows docs/CL37-sessions.jsonl --only`.

## Doing less, or spending fewer tokens?
Each session's work is now measured too. For past sessions it comes from the commits carrying its `Claude-Session` trailer in Harmonize and the kit: 195 of the 254 sessions have commits (`usage.py work-from-git`). From now on it is the same for a cloud session: the commits carrying its own trailer, plus the tests it ran and its Done checks. A computer's CLI session, which has no trailer, counts its branch's commits during its run that carry no other session's trailer. Medians per session, before vs after the cut:

| | part | board/kit part | orchestrator |
|---|---|---|---|
| cost $ | 10.20 vs 7.52 | 10.43 vs 6.92 | 22.52 vs 35.42 |
| commits | 6 vs 5.5 | 5 vs 5 | 20 vs 17.5 |
| lines changed | 756 vs 969 | 859 vs 1060 | 187 vs 1765 |
| $ per commit | 1.68 vs 1.76 (+5%) | 1.96 vs 1.76 (-10%) | 1.12 vs 1.83 (+63%) |
| $ per 100 lines changed | 1.33 vs 0.92 (-31%) | 1.29 vs 0.91 (-30%) | 11.57 vs 1.67 |
| n (with commits) | 96 vs 20 | 10 vs 19 | 26 vs 5 |

So a part is not doing less: about as many commits and more lines, for about 30% less per line. An orchestrator spends 63% more per commit. Its lines jumped because it now commits prompts and logs through the kit's scripts, so lines are a poor measure for it. Lines also count generated and data files.

## The cut

The board's update = Harmonize moving onto the kit's Artifact board page and the kit's scripts and hooks:
`d3571da` 2026-11-23 00:27 UTC (the kit's board page built for Harmonize's Artifact), `90ec38d` 01:10 (the kit's
scripts in `.kit/`, Artifact mode), `b15d577` 01:25 (`install.py --update` from the kit, nothing of Harmonize's kept
back). **Before** = sessions started at or before 00:27; **after** = sessions started at or after 01:25 (the 58
minutes between are in neither). Orchestrators O40-O48 are before; O49-O53 after (O49 is the session titled
"Harmonize orchestrator (started by the clerk)", 01:28). No orchestrator ran between O48's end (2026-11-20 08:00)
and O49.

## What the whole project spent, window against window

| window | days | parts | all sessions $ | $ a day | orchestrator + clerk $ per part | all $ per part |

| before: O40-O48, 11-17 08:56 to 11-20 08:00 | 2.96 | 33 | 848 | 286 | 7.30 | 25.69 |

"all $" counts parts, orchestrators, clerks, reviews and the rest started in the window.

## What changed

- **A part costs less**: median $10.20 a part session before (n 107) against $7.52 after (n 20), -26%; output
  tokens -35%, cache read -31%, wall time -57%. Like with like (board and kit parts): $10.43 (n 10) against $6.92
  (n 19), -34%. The after parts are shorter steps (the CL train cuts work smaller), so part of this is the step
  size, not the board.
- **An orchestrator costs more**: median $24.04 (O40-O48) against $40.32 (O49-O53), +68%; output 119k against
  207k (+74%); per hour $3.3 against $6.3. It ran ~20 parts a day instead of ~11, so per part the orchestrator and
  clerk cost $9.93 against $7.30 (+36%). Contexts end lower (O52 263k, O53 346k, against ~400k before): the 380k
  hand-over holds.
- **The whole project per part** is about the same ($22.63 against $25.69, -12%) while it spent $443 a day against
  $286: more parts a day, each a little cheaper.
- **Reviews stopped**: 15 review sessions in the before window ($106), none after. The kit's automatic reviews did
  not run as cloud sessions after the cut (or ran under titles this does not see as reviews: none named CR- or review).
- **Clerks**: $1.38 a session before (n 26), $2.02 after (n 3): too few after to say.

## Where data is missing

- **O54** (session_01AE1HGjwQKM4Sy4q6hWVWzN, running) and **CL36, CL37** (running): no usage yet; `get_session`
  shows usage only once a turn ends.
- **CL8, CL15-CL19, CL23, CL32, CL34**: no cloud session with usage under those names (run elsewhere, on a
  computer, or folded into another session's title). Their Claude Code transcripts were on the machine that ran
  them; none is on this one.
- 35 listed sessions have no usage at all (probes, `board-cl*` local sessions, ones still running).
- **Tool calls, board bytes, messages, subagents, owner turns** exist only from a transcript (`usage.py record`),
  so the before/after above has no such column: the ledger fills them from now on, for every session where the
  hook is installed.
- The cost is the platform's `cost_usd` as recorded; the 1h/5m cache-write split of past sessions is unknown.
- One window of ~1 day after the cut: medians of 6 orchestrators and 20 parts. Rerun `compare` in a week: the
  ledger will have every session's row by then without anyone fetching anything.

## The ledger, from now on

`kit.py usage` (`.kit/usage.py`, installed by `install.py`), the hook `kit_usage.py` on Stop and SessionEnd: each
session's row from its own transcript (no model call, ~0.1 s), in `.kit/run/usage/` at once and on the branch
`kit-usage` (`usage/<date>.jsonl`, git plumbing: the working tree never changes) at every Stop (a detached push: the turn never waits),
at SessionEnd and at `end_session.py`. Its fields: input, output, cache read, cache write (5m/1h) tokens, cost,
API calls, owner turns, messages sent and received, tool calls by name, kit commands run, ArtifactData reads/writes
and their bytes, board CLI calls and bytes, subagents (type, model, tokens, cost), context peak, wall and active
time, compactions, model, Claude Code version, the kit commit in force (`.kit/manifest.json` `_kit_commit`), role
and part.

## Commands checked
`kit.py commands usage|cost|token|transcript|hook|session`: nothing recorded usage. Harmonize's `scripts/board-cost.py` (M1) estimates reporting characters from saved list_events pages. The `get_session` usage it reads (`load_usage`) is the same field `usage.py import-ccr` reads. Its per-channel character split stays M1's, and is not duplicated here.

## O54's gaps, fixed
1. **The orchestrator was recorded as a part.** Its first prompt names a prompt file, and its branch read `HEAD`. Now a `HEAD` branch is ignored, a prompt file named `*orchestrator*`, `*clerk*` or `CR-*` gives that role, and a session that the board's `_orchestrator` post names is the orchestrator.
2. **Cloud records.** See Source above: no script can fetch them. The backfill was one subagent, $2.17 measured. From now on every cloud session records itself through the hook.
3. **Lost rows.** A row was already written locally at every Stop. The ledger branch is now also pushed at every Stop, detached, with a lock so pushes never overlap. A container that dies loses at most the current turn.
4. **`--before <commit>` in a shallow clone.** The commit's date now comes from the ledger rows that ran under that commit, then from `.kit/manifest.json`, then from one `--depth=1` fetch. If all three fail, the refusal says to pass a date instead.
5. **`files-board.json` and the Artifact still listed `docs/CL37.md`.** The entry and the Artifact's file document are removed.
Also fixed: Haiku 5.5's price above a 100K-token prompt ($0.50/$2.50). Without that tier the backfill agent read as $0.44.

## O55's gaps, fixed
1. **A shallow kit clone skipped the new hook.** `install.py` decided whether a hook is new from git history, which a shallow clone lacks. It now falls back to the date in the target's manifest against the date each hook entered the kit (`HOOKS_ADDED`). Rerun from a `--depth 1` kit clone on a fresh Harmonize copy (manifest 219f713): `kit_usage.py` installed and wired on Stop and SessionEnd.
2. **A role word in a part's prompt name.** Only a role's own prompt file now gives the role: `O54-orchestrator`, `BC32-board-clerk`, `CR-*`. `cl24-orchestrator-guard-gaps`, `cl28-the-orchestrator-…` and `cl5-automatic-reviews` are parts.
3. **A one-line hand-over prompt.** `--role orchestrator|clerk|review`, `.kit/claude-cli/(orchestrator|clerk|takeover).md` and "You are orchestrator N" give the role, on any branch. So does `KIT_ROLE`, which `handover.py` already sets.
4. **No work measure.** See Doing less, or spending fewer tokens? above. `compare` has rows for commits, lines changed, $ per commit, $ per 100 lines changed and tests run.

## O55's second gaps, fixed
1. **A runtime that missed the hook.** A hook listed in `HOOKS_ADDED` that the other runtime got from the kit (its manifest line) now goes into this runtime too, whatever the dates or the kit clone's history. O55's case, rerun: a `--depth 1` kit clone updating Harmonize at fd0ab576 (manifest 99f6ccf, `kit_usage.py` in `.agents` only). It wrote `.claude/hooks/kit/kit_usage.py`, and settings.json has it on Stop and SessionEnd. The rule is limited to `HOOKS_ADDED`: copying every agy-only hook broke CL28's install tests.
2. **`git_work` counted other sessions' commits.** A cloud session's work is now only the commits carrying its own trailer. The hook reads the session id from `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` (`cse_X` becomes `session_X`). Shallow-boundary commits are skipped (read from `.git/shallow`). This session's row on the copy: 8 commits, 11 files, +3305/-506 lines, by trailer.
3. **"Run kit.py resume, then read post _handover".** A `post _handover` or `post _orchestrator` pointer is the orchestrator. So is the `_orchestrator` post naming this session's cloud id.

## O55's third gap, fixed
Run inside a cloud session, the suite failed one test: the real `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` reached a fixture's row. Three changes:
- `run_all_tests.py` now clears that variable along with the other session variables.
- `usage.py` takes the cloud id only when `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` equals the transcript's own session id, so a test or a backfill run inside a cloud session never borrows it.
- The test sets a foreign cloud id on purpose.

Result: 11 of 11 suites passed in this cloud session.

## The review's redirect, items 1 and 2 done
1. **The kit's own repo records now.** `install.py --update` ran on anlonlt/board (commit fb167f8). `.claude/settings.json` has `kit_usage.py` on Stop and SessionEnd, and `.claude/hooks/kit/kit_usage.py` is there. The next session started in this repo writes its row without being asked. The update also wired the guards it was missing (`kit_board_guard.py`, `kit_cards_reminder.py`).
2. **Two-repo sessions record themselves.** A session started on two repos reads neither repo's settings, so no project hook runs. Now every `kit.py` command, `end_session.py` and `web_takeover.py save` run `usage.py self`, detached and at most once a minute. It finds the session's own transcript (`~/.claude/projects/*/<CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID>.jsonl`) and records the row. Every role runs kit commands, the orchestrator most of all. Tested on a fixture transcript: one `kit.py commands` writes the row.
- **The ledger branch exists.** `git ls-remote origin kit-usage` gives 4fe6c2e and later. Its first row was written by `end_session.py`, not by hand: this session, part CL37, 10 commits by trailer.
- Fixed on the way: a session's commits are counted in the project the row is recorded for. This session's transcript `cwd` had moved to `/home/user`, which gave 0 commits.
- Fixed on the way: `test_install_present_runtimes` failed on main after CL38 wired the message guard. It allows `kit_say_it_once.py`, and main carried the same fix.
3. **Three hook-written rows** (part, orchestrator, review, from sessions that never mentioned usage): O56 collects them, as agreed.

title: Usage ledger: tokens, tools, agents per session, recorded without tokens; before/after the board's update
verdict: Every session now records its tokens, cost, tools and work with no model call; across the board's update a part costs 31% less per line changed for as many commits, and an orchestrator 63% more per commit.
